rejected.title: Benefits of regular aerobic exercise
card: Aerobic exercise, such as running, swimming or cycling, is steady exercise that uses oxygen to supply energy. Doing it regularly over weeks and months can cause lasting changes in the body.
The heart muscle can get stronger. It can pump more blood with each beat, so it can deliver the same blood supply with fewer beats.
The breathing muscles can get stronger, and more capillaries (tiny blood vessels) can form around the muscles and lungs. More oxygen can then be taken in and delivered to working muscles.
With more oxygen delivered, a trained person can keep up exercise for longer before tiring.
rejected.remember: Regular aerobic exercise can build the heart and lungs, so more oxygen reaches the muscles.

a.q: After months of regular running, Sam's heart pumps more blood with each beat. What is the result?
opts: More oxygen reaches his working muscles
His muscles need less oxygen at any speed
His muscles tire sooner during a long run
His heart beats faster when he is resting
a.why: A stronger heart moves more blood per beat, and that blood carries oxygen, so more oxygen reaches the muscles. The option about needing less oxygen is tempting, but the benefit is better delivery, not lower demand.
a.clue: More blood per beat carries what to the muscles?

b.q: Lena has swum three times a week for six months. She now finishes a long swim without tiring as early as before. Which change best explains this?
opts: More oxygen is delivered to her working muscles
Her muscles now need no oxygen to make energy
Her lungs now hold less air with each breath
Her body now makes less use of her blood supply
b.why: Regular aerobic training can increase how much oxygen is taken in and delivered, so muscles can keep working for longer. Aerobic exercise still uses oxygen to supply energy, so the muscles do not stop needing it.
b.clue: What do muscles need to keep making energy during aerobic exercise?

flags: Question b, wording: The stem mentions 'resting heart rate', and the right option is the only one that mentions the heart. The clue ('Which change is in the heart itself?') points straight at it too, so a student can match the word without understanding the idea.
Question a, wording: The distractor 'His heart must beat faster at rest' uses 'must', while the card uses 'can'. It is a wrong option, but 'must' is on the flagged word list.

b.q: Two friends start training. Lena swims three times a week for six months. Jo does no exercise. Who is likely to keep exercising for longer before tiring?
opts: Lena, because her heart and lungs deliver more oxygen
Jo, because her heart is resting and saving oxygen
Lena, because swimming removes the need for oxygen
Jo, because her muscles are not yet tired at all
b.why: Regular swimming strengthens Lena's heart and lungs, so more oxygen reaches her muscles and she tires later. Jo's lack of exercise does not save anything, because her heart and lungs have not been trained.
b.clue: Think about who has trained heart and lungs.

a.best: More oxygen can be delivered to his muscles

b.best: Lena, because her heart and lungs deliver more oxygen
